questions.stem: How is the fascia iliaca compartment best described anatomically?
Which spinal levels supply the femoral nerve blocked by a fascia iliaca block?
Which thigh compartment does the femoral nerve supply, as blocked by a fascia iliaca block?
Which spinal levels supply the lateral cutaneous nerve of thigh in a fascia iliaca block?
Which skin area does the lateral cutaneous nerve of thigh supply, as blocked by fascia iliaca block?
Why can a large fascia iliaca volume block nerves even when injected away from them?
questions.answer: Both nerves run under the fascia iliaca, so the spread can reach them.

questions.stem: How many compartments does the fascia iliaca create under the inguinal ligament?
What is the evidence for a fascia iliaca block spreading proximally to the lumbar plexus?
questions.answer: Traditionally assumed, but not consistently shown.

questions.stem: Why are intravascular injection and nerve injury very unlikely with a fascia iliaca block?
questions.answer: The injection site is far from vessels and nerves.

questions.stem: What dilute local anaesthetic is an example for a fascia iliaca block?
What needle length is suggested for a fascia iliaca block?
Which needle bevel helps feel the fascial pops in a fascia iliaca block?
Which ultrasound transducer is used for a fascia iliaca block?
What patient position is used for an infrainguinal fascia iliaca ultrasound block?
questions.answer: Supine, with the bed flat to expose the groin.

questions.stem: How is the linear probe placed for an infrainguinal fascia iliaca block?
questions.answer: Transverse, at and parallel to the femoral crease, lateral to the femoral artery.

questions.stem: Where is the target for an infrainguinal fascia iliaca ultrasound block?
questions.answer: Under the fascia iliaca, at the lateral third of the ASIS to pubic tubercle line, several cm lateral to the artery.

questions.stem: What test volume confirms the plane between fascia and iliopsoas in a fascia iliaca block?
How much local anaesthetic volume do adults usually need for a fascia iliaca block?
In which patients may an out-of-plane fascia iliaca approach suit best?
What advantages does the suprainguinal fascia iliaca approach have?
questions.answer: More targeted, needs less volume, and eases catheter placement.

questions.stem: Where is the probe placed for the suprainguinal fascia iliaca approach?
questions.answer: High-frequency linear, parasagittal, just inferior and medial to the ASIS.

questions.stem: What needle length is used for the suprainguinal fascia iliaca approach?
Where should the needle enter relative to the inguinal ligament in the suprainguinal fascia iliaca approach?
questions.answer: 1 cm cephalad to the inguinal ligament, in-plane, directed cranially.

questions.stem: How far beyond the needle tip should a fascia iliaca catheter be advanced?
Which fascia iliaca catheter dosing may give better spread than a fixed infusion?
Why is success with the landmark fascia iliaca technique inconsistent?
Where is the landmark insertion point for a fascia iliaca block?
questions.answer: 1 cm below the junction of the lateral third and medial two-thirds of the ASIS to pubic tubercle line.
